title: Etale splitting of a finite morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite
morphism, and let $\bar s$ be a
geometric point of $S$.
There are a pointed etale neighborhood $V\to S$ of $\bar s$ and a
decomposition

$$
X\times_SV=X_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup X_m
$$

into open-and-closed $V$-subschemes, with $m$ the number of geometric
points of the finite fibre $X_{\bar s}$, such that every $X_i\to V$ is
finite and the geometric fibre $(X_i)_{\bar v}$ over the lifted point
$\bar v$ of $V$ is connected.

proof.text:
The morphism $f$ is finite in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], hence affine; replacing $S$ by an
affine open through which $\bar s$ factors we may assume
$S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C$ a
finite $R$-algebra. Let $A=\mathcal O^{{\mathrm{sh}}}_{S,\bar s}$ be
the strict henselization of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit],
the filtered colimit of the rings $A_V$ of the affine pointed etale
neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$. The scheme
$X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the spectrum of the finite
$A$-algebra $B=C\otimes_RA=\varinjlim_V C\otimes_RA_V$. The ring $A$
is strictly henselian local (Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.155.10,
Tag [04GQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04GQ)), so the finite
$A$-algebra $B$ is a finite product $B=B_1\times\cdots\times B_m$ of
local rings (Algebra, Lemma 10.153.3 (10), Tag
[04GG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04GG)). The residue field
of each $B_i$ is finite over the separably closed residue field of $A$,
hence purely inseparable over it, so each factor contributes exactly
one geometric point to the finite fibre $X_{\bar s}$ in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; thus $m$ is the number of geometric
points of $X_{\bar s}$.

Let $e_1,\dots,e_m\in B$ be the factor idempotents. Each comes from
$C\otimes_RA_V$ for some $V$, and the finitely many relations
$e_i^2=e_i$, $e_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$ and $\sum_ie_i=1$ hold after
passing to a further neighbourhood, since $B$ is the filtered colimit of
the $C\otimes_RA_V$. Over such a $V$ the idempotents decompose
$X\times_SV=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_RA_V)$ as
$X_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup X_m$ into open-and-closed subschemes, each
$X_i\to V$ is finite (a closed subscheme of the finite $V$-scheme
$X\times_SV$), and the geometric fibre $(X_i)_{\bar v}$ is the single
geometric point contributed by $B_i$, hence connected.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite morphism and let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$
be a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Call a pointed etale
neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$ *split* if it comes with a decomposition
$$
X\times_SV=\bigsqcup_{\bar x}X_{\bar x}
$$
into pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subschemes indexed by the points $\bar x$
of the finite geometric fibre of $f$ over $\bar s$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre],
such that $X_{\bar x}$ contains the point $(\bar v,\bar x)$ of $X\times_SV$. Then
every pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s$ is refined by a split one: for
every $(U,\bar u)$ there are a split neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ and a morphism
$(V,\bar v)\to(U,\bar u)$ of pointed etale neighbourhoods. Each piece
$X_{\bar x}\to V$ is finite, being a closed subscheme of the finite $V$-scheme
$X\times_SV$.

proof.text:
The morphism $f$ is finite in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], hence affine. Given $(U,\bar u)$, replace
$U$ by an affine open neighbourhood of the image of $\bar u$ lying over an
affine open of $S$; we may assume $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and
$X\times_SU=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C$ a finite $R$-algebra. Let
$A=\mathcal O^{{\mathrm{sh}}}_{U,\bar u}$ be the strict henselization of
[def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the filtered colimit of the rings
$A_V$ of the affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $(U,\bar u)$.
The ring $A$ is strictly henselian local (Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma
10.155.10, Tag [04GQ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04GQ)), so the
finite $A$-algebra $B=C\otimes_RA=\varinjlim_VC\otimes_RA_V$ is a finite product
$B=B_1\times\cdots\times B_m$ of local rings (Algebra, Lemma 10.153.3 (10), Tag
[04GG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04GG)). The residue field of each
$B_k$ is finite over the separably closed residue field of $A$, hence purely
inseparable over it; as $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, each factor has
exactly one $\Omega$-point over $\bar s$. This gives a bijection between the
factors and the points $\bar x$ of the geometric fibre
[def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre], the factor $B_{\bar x}$ being the one through
which $\bar x$ factors.

Let $e_{\bar x}\in B$ be the factor idempotents. Each comes from $C\otimes_RA_V$
for some $V$, and the finitely many relations $e_{\bar x}^2=e_{\bar x}$,
$e_{\bar x}e_{\bar x'}=0$ for $\bar x\ne\bar x'$, $\sum e_{\bar x}=1$ and
$\bar x^*(e_{\bar x'})=\delta_{\bar x\bar x'}$ hold after passing to a further
neighbourhood, since $B$ is the filtered colimit of the $C\otimes_RA_V$. Over
such a $V$ the basic opens of the idempotents decompose
$X\times_SV=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_RA_V)$ into pairwise disjoint
open-and-closed pieces $X_{\bar x}$, with $(\bar v,\bar x)\in X_{\bar x}$. The
structure map $V\to U$ is the required morphism of pointed neighbourhoods.
Finally $X_{\bar x}\to V$ is finite, as a closed subscheme of the finite
$V$-scheme $X\times_SV$.
